What are the Marilyns?

The Marilyns are the 1,550 hills in Britain with at least 150 metres of drop on all sides, whatever their height. The list was devised by Alan Dawson in 1992 and named as a play on Munro. Because it is defined by prominence alone, it includes both Ben Nevis and small coastal hills a few hundred feet high.

Make the list your own

Browse by area to find summits in the places you want to explore. Height is only one part of choosing a walk; terrain, route and conditions matter too.

In WayMark, mark the summits you have reached and keep your walking memories alongside your progress. Hills that belong to more than one list count towards each relevant list.

How many Marilyns are there?

This list contains 1,550 summits. British hills with a drop of at least 150 m on all sides, regardless of absolute height.

What is the highest summit on this list?

Ben Nevis is the highest, at 4,413 feet (1,345 metres), in Glen Coe & Lochaber.

Can I get a free Marilyns checklist?

Yes. Use Print checklist on this page for a paper copy of all 1,550 summits, or open the list in WayMark to keep a digital record for free.
